title: KISS wearable-to-runtime-root TAVRN dashboard PoC
goal: Integrate the 1000 ms wearable spray with corrected FULL TAVRN using a separate Layer-7 MIND application: each backbone suppresses local spray copies for 2000 ms, the application projects read-only GTT topology into its own fixed root registry and fans first-seen packets to every designated root, and a local serial API feeds a globally deduplicating dashboard. TAVRN remains an unchanged flat opaque-data mesh; two roots is only a competition soft cap.
scope: Reconcile origin/master, recent fall-shout wearable behavior, and corrected FULL TAVRN on a dedicated integration branch while preserving TAVRN protocol sources
Preserve the wearable stable 24-bit packet identity across its 1000 ms spray
Classify direct TM/01 wearable advertisements into an application RX plane before TAVRN dispatch
Add exact 2000 ms per-node suppression with bounded transactional ingress
Add a read-only topology projection from copied GTT snapshots into Layer-7 application records without mutating or specializing GTT
Add runtime UART ROOT ON/OFF/STATUS; local designation lasts until reboot and is independent of TAVRN
Maintain root freshness in an application-owned fixed registry and announce local root state through existing generic opaque TAVRN DATA plus application-level ACK
Treat two simultaneous roots only as the recommended competition/demo soft cap; firmware application fanout, API devices, and dashboard state support the full application registry
Send an inactive current-session announcement after SID8 establishment when a rebooted node is not a root, preventing stale application root state without leases
Fan each first-seen wearable report independently to every active application root through one Layer-7 arbiter and existing generic TAVRN DATA submission
Clear application roots and retained event targets on accepted ROOT OFF or explicit copied GTT departure
Provide persistent node-number/root-presence display and a cockpit-style cue on local root transition
Emit exact machine-readable event/root/command records on root UARTs
Add a minimal bidirectional repeated-serial localhost API and small dashboard with session-global dedupe
Validate host behavior, unchanged TAVRN protocol hashes/regressions, production builds/resources, mandatory rootless/one-root/two-root hardware flows, and software fanout to application capacity
nonGoals: MQTT, MQTT-SN, ESP32-C3, ESP-MESH-LITE, broker integration, cloud connectivity, or protocol compliance claims
Automatic root election, priority arbitration, consensus, split-brain prevention, or root failover; UART designation is explicit and any bounded number of roots may coexist
Periodic application root leases; TAVRN/GTT departure is the root-loss authority
End-to-end event application acknowledgments, exactly-once delivery, durable storage, reboot persistence, or production sessions
Buffering wearable events while the root registry is empty; rootless events are consumed after application ingress without user-facing output
RF hardening, radio-driver changes, scheduler redesign, duty-cycle optimization, or mitigation of RX exhaustion caused by TX activity
Changes to TAVRN membership, GTT, AODV, HACK, repair, mentorship, or maintenance semantics
Production security, provisioning, encryption, authentication, or a general-purpose application framework
constraints: This is a KISS competition PoC: fixed records, bounded application tables, one mesh-owner application arbiter, and no speculative framework

Layer separation is strict: TAVRN/GTT exposes copied topology and routes opaque application DATA; ROOT_STATE, ROOT_ACK, MIND_REPORT, root limits, retries, UI, and dedupe exist only in the MIND application layer
All corrected TAVRN protocol sources under microbit/app/protocol/tavrn_*.{c,h}, including wire/router/GTT/full/ESC semantics, remain byte-identical to 49e2ee8 during application slices

Application kinds 0x02..0x04 and exact payload validation live in mind_application headers/code. TAVRN performs only its existing generic DATA width/length validation and must not learn root or report semantics
Wearables remain outside TAVRN; recognized TM/01 MIND_EVENT frames are consumed as direct application ingress and never legacy-relayed
Each wearable logical message reuses one packet ID24 throughout its 1000 ms spray
Each backbone node commits a valid wearable key at most once for exactly 2000 ms with wrap-safe equality expiry
Ingress validates, reserves cache and queue, copies, then commits; failures leave the key unseen, but after commit downstream BUSY never removes the seen key
All valid first-seen classes enter the application queue; zero active application roots causes silent consume with only an internal counter
Define MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY=16 as an independent Layer-7 static array size. It includes local and remote root records; it is not derived from, exported to, or asserted equal to TAVRN_GTT_CAPACITY
Root designation is RAM-only; every node exposes a current local root-state tuple using the router existing boot nonce and nonzero application generation
Application root history has MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY entries with no live eviction; the active-root set is a view over this application table, never a TAVRN structure or separate two-entry index
Two roots is only a recommended demo/UI soft cap and must not appear in TAVRN, wire, fanout, API, or dashboard collection bounds

The application topology adapter consumes copied routed_full_telemetry GTT snapshots and resolver results through existing public seams. It copies canonical identities/freshness/departure into application-owned records and never mutates, extends, or interprets GTT storage as root state

The frozen topology snapshot seam exposes only OK or non-OK, not truncation. Non-OK preserves all application state, increments snapshot-failure evidence, and retries later; a full returned snapshot is never inferred to be truncated. Application registry/campaign capacity is tested independently

An unknown ROOT_STATE rejected because the application registry is full is not retained in a hidden rejection cache. Every repeated delivery is reevaluated against current capacity and receives capacity-rejected only while capacity remains full
ROOT_STATE and ROOT_ACK are ordinary generic SID8 DATA. Commands before SID8 update local application role/UI immediately and defer campaigns until SID8 readiness
Application campaign and event-target capacities are independently defined fixed application constants, initially 16, and use explicit count/overflow behavior. They are not TAVRN constants

Resolver UNIQUE attempts generic DATA submission. UNKNOWN or COLLIDING retains the application obligation and retries after later topology snapshots/rediscovery. RESERVED or INVALID is fail-closed with application invariant evidence and no submission/removal
Accepted/duplicate ROOT_ACK completes application success; capacity/stale completes rejected; no ACK remains retryable; ACK must resolve to the exact target and match all echoed state bytes
Application roots and per-event targets clear on accepted newer OFF or explicit copied GTT departed=true; no application lease exists
Leaf display uses zero/one/two-or-more visual states and saturates at two LEDs; saturation is presentation-only and never truncates exact application root count or fanout

One mesh-owner application arbiter selects exactly one ROOT_ACK, urgent report, ROOT_STATE, or heartbeat per existing application-submit phase and correlates the result to one retained application owner
Each ingress item snapshots all active roots using a MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY target set. Target progress is independent and root removal clears only matching targets
Generic final DATA remains in its reserved application inbox until Layer-7 processing or logger-record reservation succeeds; logger never mutates application root state
The application MIND_REPORT preserves wearable ID, packet ID24, and unchanged schema-v1 payload in exact ten-byte generic SID8 DATA
UART commands use an application-owned 32-byte RX-only interrupt ring installed after inherited device startup; T-monitor remains sole TX owner and kernel/radio/scheduler files are unchanged
New application modules perform no dynamic allocation; application queues/state/PWM/UI/UART rings are static. Inherited kernel task/device startup allocation is unchanged and not claimed heap-free

The plan requires compile-time sizeof reports and measured aggregate .data/.bss deltas for every new fixed application structure, declared fixed-state allowance updates from evidence, at least 8192 bytes post-reserve RAM, at least 1024 bytes mesh-stack headroom, and maximum-application-capacity builds. By explicit user decision after callsite-complete evidence, the inherited mesh chain ceiling/allocation/reserve are revised to 4096/4864/13360 bytes rather than refactoring frozen behavior
Production manifests prove FULL repair-on/ingress/node number and benchmark/hooks/diagnostic initiator/RF blocks off; they do not contain a TAVRN root role
The host bridge accepts repeated serial arguments without a semantic two-device cap, passes duplicates unchanged, and gives every path a stable process-lifetime device index
Dashboard collections and root controls are dynamic over API devices; dashboard alone deduplicates events by wearable ID and packet ID24
Frozen radio/scheduler and TAVRN protocol files remain byte-identical to 49e2ee8; RX starvation under TX load remains deferred
A slice is a higher-level deliverable. Each slice contains one or more explicit waves; a wave launches its non-overlapping writers, then exactly one checker reviews the combined wave output
Checkers review waves, never individual writer outputs. Valid checker findings are fixed within the same wave and receive only the necessary consolidated recheck before advancement

phases.title: Slice A — reproducible source reconciliation and production baseline

steps.title: Wave A1 — reconcile pinned sources and production profile
steps.target: git history, submodule, build layout, source closure and manifest tests
steps.action: One code-writer owns serial reconciliation: start from origin/master@648efe4, merge corrected TAVRN 49e2ee8, preserve wearable/schema and every frozen TAVRN protocol/radio/scheduler file, selectively port wearable 74d4931 without driver relocation/old flood, and define production application ingress/node-number source closure. The writer owns CMake/profile registration during baseline. Then one code-checker reviews the complete Wave A1 diff; valid fixes remain in Wave A1 and receive one consolidated recheck.
steps.validation: Pinned refs/submodule/frozen TAVRN protocol/radio/scheduler hashes/source list/manifests are exact; no C3/MQTT/old flood/benchmark contamination; wearable and inherited TAVRN baseline tests/builds pass; Wave A1 checker approves.

phases.title: Slice B — direct wearable ingress and 2000 ms suppression

steps.title: Wave B1 — freeze Layer-7 records and implement wearable ingress
steps.target: shared schema, mind_application packet codec/contracts, wearable transport, ingress/cache and focused tests
steps.action: Launch three non-overlapping code-writers: writer B1a owns shared schema comments plus new mind_application packet constants/codec/docs/golden vectors and does not edit tavrn protocol files; writer B1b owns wearable source/CMake/tx tests; writer B1c owns new application ingress files, routed-cycle/main integration, profile registration for this slice, and ingress tests. After all settle, one code-checker reviews the combined Wave B1 diff; fixes and one consolidated recheck stay in this wave.
steps.validation: Application codec proves exact MIND_REPORT/ROOT_STATE/ROOT_ACK records over existing generic SID8 DATA; TAVRN protocol hashes stay unchanged; exact TM/01 TTL-zero ingress, 1000 ms wearable spray, validate/reserve/copy/commit rollback, 2000 ms behavior, no legacy relay and no TAVRN mutation pass; Wave B1 checker approves.

phases.title: Slice C — Layer-7 topology projection, runtime roots, UART command, ACK campaign, and UI

steps.title: Wave C1 — implement application topology and root plane
steps.target: mind_application topology adapter/root registry/campaign, UART command, display/speaker, integration and focused tests
steps.action: One code-writer owns the complete Layer-7 root slice. It implements a read-only GTT-to-application topology adapter, independent 16-entry MIND root registry/campaign state, ACK/arbiter APIs, UART RX command module, UI/speaker modules, routed main/CMake/test registration, and focused tests. It only calls existing generic TAVRN snapshot/resolver/submit seams and edits no tavrn protocol file. One code-checker reviews the complete Wave C1 diff; valid fixes and one consolidated recheck remain in Wave C1.
steps.validation: Application registry 0/1/2/16/full+1 boundaries, repeated capacity rejection then acceptance after a slot frees, topology snapshot OK/non-OK preservation and retry, retained unresolved roots/rediscovery, exact active counts, ACK correlation, campaigns, UART vector coexistence, saturated two-LED presentation, cue, priorities and resources pass; TAVRN protocol hashes/regressions remain unchanged; Wave C1 checker approves.

phases.title: Slice D — Layer-7 event fanout and root UART delivery

steps.title: Wave D1 — implement all-root application fanout and truthful final delivery
steps.target: mind_application event target set/arbiter, generic final inbox/logger records and tests
steps.action: One code-writer owns application event fanout and final delivery: MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY target snapshots, one-submit arbiter integration, generic local/remote DATA submission, final inbox/logger ownership, UART records and tests. It uses existing router reserve/commit/cancel and generic DATA unchanged; no tavrn protocol file is edited. One code-checker reviews the complete Wave D1 diff; fixes and one consolidated recheck stay in D1.
steps.validation: Boundary matrix covers zero/one/two/16 application roots, exact counts, one event with all application targets independently progressing, matching OFF/departure-only clearing, over-capacity preservation/rejection, unresolved rediscovery, generic DATA/HACK/BUSY/duplicate truth and UART records; all TAVRN protocol files remain byte-identical; Wave D1 checker approves.

steps.title: Wave D2 — close measured application memory and stack budgets
steps.target: build-tavrn-ble.sh, resource checker/fixtures/manifests and maximum-application-capacity build evidence
steps.action: One code-writer owns resource closure after D1. It reports sizeof for application root/campaign/event/final/logger/UART/UI structures, measures production .data/.bss delta, and builds/tests MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY=16. Callsite-complete evidence revises the inherited mesh chain ceiling/allocation/runtime reserve to 4096/4864/13360 bytes while retaining independent >=1024 mesh headroom and >=8192 post-reserve RAM gates. Because the historical FAST/BALANCED six-file baseline was lost and the user explicitly waived recovery, D2 adds an explicit paired D2_APPLICATION_INCREMENTAL mode: build FULL+repair BALANCED node 6 ingress OFF, pass its current gate, then externally seal its artifact manifest before building ingress ON. Both artifacts use hashed callsite-complete v3 routed-mesh contracts; v2 is invalid for every production FULL mesh invocation, including ingress OFF/ON, stack-baseline-only, live-resource, and retained legacy FAST/BALANCED callers. The exact ON source additions are display.c plus mind_application wire, ingress, event_forwarder, topology_adapter, root_plane, root_coordinator, root_inbox, command, log, log_formatter, uart, audio, and ui; no source removal or common-file hash change is allowed. The build-config header may differ only by TRON_BUILD_ENABLE_WEARABLE_INGRESS 0->1. The build-config manifest may differ semantically only by adding mind-root-plane capability, wearable_ingress requested/effective OFF->ON, root_plane OFF->ON, and the exact selected-source list/hash additions. Repair, timer, node number, capacities, hooks, benchmark, stack allocations, reserve, source state, and every other semantic field are identical. Artifact/resource hashes and application evidence sidecars may differ only as independently hash-bound consequences of those additions. The ON comparison requires exact ELF symbol accounting and publishes acceptance.scope=D2_APPLICATION_INCREMENTAL plus historical_expiry_fixed_state=USER_WAIVED_NOT_REPRODUCED; it must not masquerade as historical expiry acceptance. TAVRN protocol capacities/sources remain unchanged. One code-checker reviews the amended Wave D2.
steps.validation: Per-structure/aggregate bytes and exact OFF-to-ON deltas pass; OFF is externally sealed only after its current gate passes and ON is compared afterward; both artifact manifests record resource.gate=PASSED. Pair validation proves zero removals/common-source hash changes, exactly the fourteen allowed source additions, only the one generated-header and four semantic build-manifest changes, and unchanged repair/timer/node/capacities/hooks/benchmark/stack/reserve/source state. Every production FULL routed_mesh_task path rejects v2 and uses published/hashed callsite-complete v3 evidence. Measured mesh chain is <=4096 and allocation-minus-chain is >=1024 independently (effective maximum 3840); post-reserve RAM is >=8192 with reserve 13360; unexplained application delta is <=512; no hidden application heap or frozen TAVRN source change; the paired report hashes both artifacts, external seal, checker outputs, preprocessed mains, contracts, and size report, and explicitly marks historical expiry fixed-state evidence user-waived and not reproduced; Wave D2 checker approves.

phases.title: Slice E — bidirectional local serial API and KISS dashboard

steps.title: Wave E1 — implement repeated-serial API and dynamic dashboard
steps.target: host bridge, parser/API tests, dashboard API/store/UI/tests
steps.action: Launch two parallel non-overlapping code-writers: E1a owns the Python repeated-serial bridge/tests; E1b owns dashboard files, dynamic device/root collections, global dedupe and frontend tests/build. No firmware application capacity leaks into API/dashboard contracts. One code-checker reviews the combined host wave; fixes and one consolidated recheck stay in E1.
steps.validation: One/two/16 mocked serial devices get stable indices and serialized writes; exact API/error/cursor contracts pass; dashboard dynamically controls roots and deduplicates multi-root/multi-observer reports with no hard firmware-cap assumption, MQTT or C3; accessibility checks pass; Wave E1 checker approves.

phases.title: Slice F — complete regression and competition hardware proof

steps.title: Wave F1 — run complete software/source/resource gates
steps.action: Launch two non-overlapping validation/fix writers. F1a owns firmware/application/tests/build/resource scripts only; F1b owns dashboard/host bridge only. After tests/builds/resource/source assertions settle, one code-checker reviews the combined implementation and evidence once; valid findings receive one consolidated recheck.
steps.validation: All focused/inherited tests, application capacity matrix, firmware builds/manifests/resources, frozen TAVRN protocol/radio/scheduler hashes, submodule/source assertions, dynamic host tests/build/rendered checks and diff hygiene pass; Wave F1 checker approves.

steps.title: Wave F2 — execute competition hardware proof and final handoff
steps.target: one wearable, at least three backbone nodes, mandatory two concurrent root UART captures
steps.action: Rerun the mandatory rootless, one-root, and two-root/two-UART hardware flows using current committed firmware and dashboard. Persist redacted logs, manifests, API output, screenshots, checksums, and exact artifact provenance under microbit/hardware-results before marking complete.
steps.validation: Persistent repository evidence—not tmpfs paths—proves rootless/one/two hardware, typed campaigns/UI/fanout/dashboard dedupe, withdrawal, and no terminal faults. Checksums and reproduction instructions pass after reboot.

steps.title: Wave F2a — diagnose ROOT OFF and terminal-fault context without changing TAVRN
steps.target: mind UART/coordinator integration and routed-node application diagnostics
steps.action: Reproduce the post-ROOT-ON command failure in focused tests or hardware instrumentation, add bounded Layer-7 diagnostics for the AODV_STATUS_INVALID source path, and fix only defects outside frozen TAVRN.
steps.validation: Focused application/UART tests pass; required TAVRN files remain byte-identical; hardware logs identify ROOT OFF processing and the exact router-tick invalid branch.

steps.title: Wave F2b — add an explicitly test-only wearable event injector
steps.target: wearable_app build configuration and focused tests
steps.action: Add a compile-time-disabled production-safe injector that emits a deterministic non-heartbeat incident through the existing 1000 ms spray path for hardware acceptance.
steps.validation: Default wearable artifact remains behaviorally unchanged; injector build emits one stable packet identity across the required spray copies and focused tests pass.

steps.title: Wave F2c — rerun software gates and competition hardware proof
steps.target: affected firmware gates plus pyOCD UID-targeted hardware topology
steps.action: Rerun current software gates and the full UID-targeted hardware acceptance after the GTT/dashboard and root-control changes, then persist the evidence bundle. Historical tmpfs observations may guide the run but cannot close acceptance.
steps.validation: All current software gates pass; persistent hardware evidence satisfies every competition acceptance item and remains readable/checksummed after reboot.

reviewFindings.title: History reconciliation recipe was under-specified
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved in revised plan with exact refs, corrected submodule choice, frozen-file equality, selective wearable source port, and explicit exclusion of relocation/old flood node.

reviewFindings.title: Wearable classifier and source ownership were under-specified
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by freezing the pre-mentorship RX classifier outcomes, recognized-frame consumption, exact validation, source closure, and build flag.

reviewFindings.title: Seen-cache and application queue transaction was incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with mesh-owner validate/purge/duplicate/reserve/commit ordering, fixed capacities, rollback, rootless consume, and saturation tests.

reviewFindings.title: HACK duplicate validation made an impossible byte-preservation claim
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by separating DATA byte preservation, HACK correlation, duplicate DATA, BUSY, direct-local, and multi-observer behavior.

reviewFindings.title: UART and HTTP contracts were not frozen
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with exact firmware line grammar, direct nonblocking UART command input, cursor API schemas, ring bounds, localhost binding, and same-origin serving.

reviewFindings.title: Dashboard global dedupe and UI scope were ambiguous
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by limiting UI to root/health/latest wearable/event feed and aggregating observer paths under one stable key; MQTT/node analytics are removed.

reviewFindings.title: Forwarded wire contract was tentative
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by definitively assigning application kinds 0x02..0x04 and exact byte/source/width rules.

reviewFindings.title: Validation gates lacked exact source and manifest assertions
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved in revised validation section and step validations.

reviewFindings.title: Root OFF and reboot freshness required inactive high-water
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with an independent 16-entry Layer-7 root registry retaining inactive current tuple and one prior nonce, plus current-session inactive announcement after SID8 when not designated root. Registry size is application-owned, not derived from GTT.

reviewFindings.title: Root campaigns lacked exact GTT/SID8 and ACK outcome bindings
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by pinning routed_full_telemetry snapshots, tavrn_full outgoing resolution, tavrn_esc incoming resolution, pre-SID8 deferral, terminal ACK outcomes, repeated-command campaigns, and event-target cancellation.

reviewFindings.title: Downstream BUSY contradicted committed seen suppression
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved: seen keys never roll back after ingress commit; one mesh-owner arbiter owns exactly one submit per cycle; local targets retain on BUSY and final accepted DATA stays reserved until processing/logger capacity.

reviewFindings.title: Polled UART command input could overrun at 115200
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with application-owned RXDRDY/ERROR-only interrupt ring; T-monitor retains TX and kernel submodule remains unchanged.

reviewFindings.title: Firmware/API schemas and two-serial support remained incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with exact command/event/root line grammars, record/health/POST JSON shapes and status codes, stable repeated --serial device indexing, and command records in cursor stream.

reviewFindings.title: Two-root hardware validation was optional
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by making two-root/two-UART fanout, display, bridge, dedupe, and withdrawal a mandatory hardware acceptance pass.

reviewFindings.title: Initial backoff and minimum inter-submit cadence disagreed
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with both deterministic 20..120 ms per-target initial due time and global minimum 50 ms actual ROOT_STATE submission throttle.

reviewFindings.title: Equal-generation conflict and ROOT_ACK correlation were incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by freezing conflicting equal-generation state as stale and requiring exact resolved sender/target plus six-byte campaign tuple before ACK completion.

reviewFindings.title: Root history and campaign overflow behavior was unspecified
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with no-eviction preservation, capacity-rejected unknown states including OFF, deferred new campaign targets, counters, and later snapshot retry.

reviewFindings.title: UART vector coexistence remained under-specified
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with exact application-time vector replacement after inherited device startup, priority 5 enable, RXDRDY/ERROR mask, TXDRDY disable, event/error handling, and prohibition on opening sera.

reviewFindings.title: Whole-firmware no-heap claim contradicted inherited runtime
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by limiting the static-allocation rule to new application modules and leaving inherited kernel/device startup unchanged.

reviewFindings.title: HTTP errors/defaults/concurrent serial writes were not frozen
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with exact defaults, error schema/enums, health root shape, exclusive cursor semantics, and one serialized writer queue per device.

reviewFindings.title: Dashboard source reference was not reproducible
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by pinning historical reference 0c1557e and exact scaffold/style files; application/state/API modules are authored afresh and MQTT/node analytics excluded.

reviewFindings.title: Hard two-root limit leaked across application layers
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with independent MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY=16 inside Layer 7. The separate two-entry active index is removed; TAVRN carries opaque data, serial/dashboard collections are dynamic, and two remains only a UI/demo soft cap.

reviewFindings.title: Execution model conflated writer tasks, waves, and slices
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by making phases the six slices and structured steps explicit waves. Each wave names non-overlapping writer ownership and exactly one combined-wave checker; no per-writer checker remains.

reviewFindings.title: GTT capacity was incorrectly treated as 16 remote identities plus self
reviewFindings.detail: Superseded by the stricter layer separation: corrected GTT capacity includes self, but Layer-7 root capacity is independently fixed by MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY and has no cross-layer equality contract.

reviewFindings.title: Retained roots missing from GTT had undefined progress
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by freezing resolver outcomes: UNIQUE submits; UNKNOWN/COLLIDING retains and retries after snapshots/rediscovery; RESERVED/INVALID fail closed with invariant evidence; only OFF/departure clears.

reviewFindings.title: Validation did not prove maximum root capacity
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved with 0/1/2/16/full+1 application-registry boundaries, maximum campaign/event targets, over-capacity rejection, exact counts, and 16-device bridge/dashboard fixtures independent of TAVRN capacity.

reviewFindings.title: All-root static memory was not budgeted
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by adding Wave D2 with named sizeof, measured .data/.bss, declared fixed-state, stack/headroom, maximum-capacity build and resource-gate ownership.

reviewFindings.title: Wave C1 had an unsafe parallel dependency and shared-file ambiguity
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by assigning the complete root/UART/UI integration to one writer and one combined-wave checker; other parallel waves now name exact subsystem/shared-file ownership.

reviewFindings.title: Root capacity was incorrectly modeled as a GTT/TAVRN property
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by introducing independent MIND_APP_ROOT_CAPACITY=16 inside Layer 7. GTT is now only a read-only topology input; TAVRN, API, and dashboard do not encode application root limits.

reviewFindings.title: Root application kinds and validation leaked into TAVRN protocol changes
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by moving 0x02..0x04 packet definitions/validation to mind_application and freezing all corrected tavrn protocol files. Existing generic SID8 DATA carries opaque bytes unchanged.

reviewFindings.title: Capacity-rejected root tuples had impossible duplicate history
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by storing no hidden rejection tuple. Unknown ROOT_STATE is reevaluated on every delivery and returns capacity-rejected only while the independent application registry remains full.

reviewFindings.title: Frozen GTT snapshot seam cannot report truncation
reviewFindings.detail: Resolved by treating non-OK snapshot as opaque application input failure that preserves state/counts/retries; full snapshots are never inferred truncated and application capacity is tested independently.

reviewFindings.title: Wave A1 destructively reverted current-main files
reviewFindings.detail: ESP sniffer/watch tooling and related current-main paths were deleted/reverted during tree reconciliation. Restore from pinned origin/master without removing intentional TAVRN additions.

reviewFindings.title: Wave A1 regressed hardware-validated microphone gain
reviewFindings.detail: Imported mic driver replaced current-main gain-4 behavior while wearable thresholds still assume gain 4. Restore current-main mic driver.

reviewFindings.title: Inherited scheduler startup-order gate remains red
reviewFindings.detail: Corrected TAVRN starts cyclic/mesh/logger while static gate expects logger/cyclic/mesh. This predates application integration and is being treated as explicitly named out-of-scope evidence unless Wave A1 caused it.

reviewFindings.title: Wave A1 imported unrelated historical hardware artifacts
reviewFindings.detail: Prune unreferenced captures/transcripts/failure reports; retain only executable-test inputs required by the integrated baseline.

reviewFindings.title: Shared schema comments describe obsolete C3 bare-beacon authority
reviewFindings.detail: Update comments for TM/01 carriage, ID24 application identity and compatibility seq without changing seven-byte layout.

reviewFindings.title: No host test exercises ble_emit_pack exact vector
reviewFindings.detail: Add focused host test for exact 26-byte direct-ingress packet, TTL zero, ID24 masking, source/type/schema and repeat equality.

reviewFindings.title: MIND_REPORT urgent semantics missing from Layer-7 record
reviewFindings.detail: Thread generic DATA urgent through application record, derive it in report packer, and enforce urgent iff event is non-heartbeat.

reviewFindings.title: Ingress filter timing used stale phase timestamp
reviewFindings.detail: Return validated filter completion time and use it for consumed traces and passthrough router phase start.

reviewFindings.title: Benchmark and wearable-ingress sources could coexist
reviewFindings.detail: Reject benchmark+ingress configuration and assert mutual source/manifest isolation.

reviewFindings.title: Ingress FIFO consistency validation incomplete
reviewFindings.detail: Validate tail=(head+count)%capacity and classify passthrough frames before application-state validation.

reviewFindings.title: ROOT_ACK enum lower bound not validated portably
reviewFindings.detail: Validate exact enum membership including negative casts; preserve output on rejection.

reviewFindings.title: Generated Python bytecode and stale ingress test comment
reviewFindings.detail: Add repository ignore coverage without deleting files absent explicit deletion approval; update stale source-less comment.

reviewFindings.title: MIND_REPORT urgency validator read packet-ID byte
reviewFindings.detail: Use schema event-type offset inside the 10-byte report and add vectors where packet-ID middle byte contradicts event urgency.

reviewFindings.title: Wave C1 UART ring/mailbox/error handling unsafe
reviewFindings.detail: Use race-free SPSC or interrupt-masked ownership, synchronize command mailbox, and clear ERRORSRC write-one-to-clear with interleaving/register tests.

reviewFindings.title: Root commands could mutate state without required records
reviewFindings.detail: Reserve command/root log capacity transactionally before mutation and retain attempts while output is busy; no silent mailbox/log drops.

reviewFindings.title: Failed ROOT_STATE submissions bypassed 50 ms pacing
reviewFindings.detail: Record every actual submit-seam invocation for global pacing; apply 3000 ms ACK deadline only after accepted handoff; add multi-target BUSY tests.

reviewFindings.title: UI/audio had unsynchronized multiple owners and stale time
reviewFindings.detail: Make low-priority UI task sole framebuffer/PWM owner, publish synchronized state/transition sequence, use real task clock, queue every genuine root transition and propagate display start failure.

reviewFindings.title: Wave C1 tests omitted required boundary and routed integration matrix
reviewFindings.detail: Add generation/full-table/freshness/campaign/ACK/resolver/UART/UI and routed-binding acceptance tests identified by consolidated checker.

reviewFindings.title: Wave C1 integration test bypassed production coordinator

reviewFindings.title: Pre-reset health root can override new epoch indefinitely

reviewFindings.title: Mismatched accepted root echo leaves original device pending
reviewFindings.detail: postRoot decodes but does not require response device/command to match the request. A mismatched 202 clears another device and cancels timeout, leaving the original disabled. Reject mismatched echoes so rootFailed clears the original pending state.

reviewFindings.title: Delayed pre-reset health response is tagged with the new epoch
reviewFindings.detail: Events and health start concurrently, but health dispatch reads the mutable epoch ref when it resolves. If events reset first, stale pre-reset health is mislabeled current and can override new stream root state. Capture request epoch before launching both requests and dispatch health with that immutable epoch; add delayed-health/reset race test.

reviewFindings.detail: serial_grouping_identity directly references os.path.ALLOW_MISSING. Use a portable fallback/default realpath behavior and test with the attribute absent.
